entry.title: Apple Restricts Advanced Data Protection in the UK Following Encryption Dispute
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | macanorak.com | hacker news

Apple has implemented a two-tier encryption system for iCloud users in the United Kingdom following a dispute with the UK government. While existing users who enabled Advanced Data Protection (ADP) retain end-to-end encryption for various sensitive data categories, Apple has prevented new UK users from activating the feature. This follows a reported Technical Capability Notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which requested that Apple ensure the technical capability to access encrypted data.

The decision stems from Apple's refusal to implement a "master key" or backdoor, maintaining its policy that weakening encryption for one purpose compromises all users. The dispute has led to legal challenges in the Investigatory Powers Tribunal and prompted U.S. lawmakers to criticize the use of secret orders that potentially impact global technology standards. The current arrangement creates a security disparity for UK residents based on whether they opted into ADP before the restriction.
